nutrient transceptors for macro- and micro-nutrients are a rapidly expanding world in eukaryotes, including human cells, and that they have important functions in the control of diverse cellular properties.
nutrient transceptors have been found to control diverse cellular properties in many eukaryotes, including human cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the yeast PKA pathway is regulated by the presence or absence of a specific macro- or micro- nutrient in the medium and that this is accomplished through the activity of a specific high-affinity transporter that acts as a nutrient transceptor.
the yeast PKA pathway is controlled by nutrient transceptors for macro- and micro-nutrients, which are the most abundant and diverse nutrients in the medium.

the nutrient composition of the growth medium has dramatic effects not only on the specific responses to starvation, but also on the regulation of diverse cellular properties, like storage levels, stress tolerance, growth rate, etc.
The main takeaway from our work is that
transceptors are widespread in eukaryotes, including human cells, and are likely to be the major nutrient sensing mechanisms for control of the PKA signaling pathway in these cells.
the PKA pathway is a major target for sensing of nutrient levels, which is not only true for yeast but is also true for many other eukaryotic organisms.
the presence of nutrients is an important environmental signal for the cell and that this is sensed by the cell via transceptors.
